basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '| Vers. 1. Adam vero cognovit uxorem suam. In paradiso positus non legitur cognovisse'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 1. Adam vero cognovit uxorem suam. In paradiso positus non legitur cognovisse uxorem suam, sed postquam ejectus est de paradiso. Quia enim peccaturus erat et mortales filios generaturus, ideo nullus ex ejus stirpe in paradiso natus est qui locus est vitae. Quae concepit et peperit dicens: possedi hominem per Deum. Cainiti Hebraice Possidere dicitur. Quia ergo mater dixit: Possedi hominem, vocatus est Cain possessio.
